name: majorana_symmetry_block_diagonalization
precondition: family = dv_angle (Clifford+Rz op list), 2 <= n_qubits <= 14, needs rotations, measurement_free. The op list must be Gaussian in the Jordan-Wigner sense: `v4.api.fermion.is_gaussian(ops)` is true, i.e. every rotation's front-frame Pauli is a Majorana bilinear i*g_a*g_b (`bilinear_of` succeeds for all of them) and the residual Clifford is a signed Majorana permutation. Fires only when the current off-grid rotation count exceeds the symmetry-reduced Givens count computed below. Circuits that are not free-fermion are excluded and cost nothing.
identity: A Gaussian circuit acts on the 2n Majoranas as one real orthogonal R in O(2n) (`orthogonal_of(ops)`); the existing free-fermion rule realises R by a plain Givens network, which needs 2n(2n-1)/2 plane rotations (66 for n=6) because that is dim SO(2n). Reduce that count with a SYMMETRY instead. Let S be a signed permutation of the Majoranas with S^2 = I (an involution). Every such S is a Gaussian Clifford (it maps Pauli strings to Pauli strings), so applying it is free of rotations. If R commutes with S, then R preserves each eigenspace V_+ , V_- of S, of dimensions d_+ + d_- = 2n. Let B be the orthogonal change of basis into those eigenspaces. Then B^T R B = R_+ (+) R_- is block diagonal, and R = B (R_+ (+) R_-) B^T. Givens-decompose each block separately: d_+(d_+ -1)/2 + d_-(d_- -1)/2 plane rotations instead of 2n(2n-1)/2. For a balanced split of 12 that is 15 + 15 = 30 instead of 66. B itself is free: the eigenvectors of an involutive signed permutation are (e_j +- S e_j)/sqrt(2) on each 2-cycle {j, S(j)} and e_j on each fixed point, so B is a product of plane rotations by exactly pi/4 in the planes (j, S(j)) -- angles on the pi/4 grid, which gridsynth never pays for (they emit Clifford/T directly through `with_ops`). Procedure: (1) R = orthogonal_of(ops); (2) enumerate a declared finite family of involutive signed Majorana permutations S -- site reflection j -> n+1-j about the chain centre, half-chain translation, global Majorana sign flips g_{2i-1} -> -g_{2i-1}, and their products -- each as a 12x12 signed permutation with S^2 = I; (3) keep those with ||R S - S R||_F < 1e-9; (4) for each kept S compute the Givens count of the block form, take the S minimising it; (5) re-emit the circuit as B, then `givens(R_+)` and `givens(R_-)` on the block coordinates, then B^T, then the residual sign diagonal, via `fermion.emit` / `plane_rotation`; (6) keep the candidate only if the off-grid rotation count strictly falls.
correctness: Exact, no error drawn. (i) The map from a Gaussian circuit to R in O(2n) is a group homomorphism and is faithful up to global phase, so reproducing the same R (and the same residual sign diagonal / parity sector) reproduces the same unitary up to global phase -- this is the same correctness argument the existing free-fermion rule already relies on, only the factorisation of R changes. (ii) [R,S] = 0 with S^2 = I implies R preserves ker(S-I) and ker(S+I), the standard isotypic decomposition (Schur); hence B^T R B is block diagonal with orthogonal blocks, exactly. (iii) B is orthogonal and is itself a signed-permutation-conjugated product of pi/4 plane rotations, so B and B^T are exactly representable with on-grid angles. (iv) Each block is realised by its own exact Givens (QR) factorisation, which is exact arithmetic on a d x d orthogonal matrix. (v) The judge still checks the whole circuit against the original: the rewrite is unitary-exact up to global phase, and the only residual error is the usual gridsynth error on the surviving rotations, which is cheaper because there are fewer of them (eps_rz = eps_synth / N_Rz actually grows, a second-order extra saving I do not claim).
trigger: `is_gaussian(ops)` is true AND R = `orthogonal_of(ops)` commutes (Frobenius residual < 1e-9) with at least one involutive signed Majorana permutation S from the declared family, whose eigenspace split (d_+, d_-) gives d_+(d_+ -1)/2 + d_-(d_- -1)/2 < (number of current off-grid rotations). On tfim_6: 66 off-grid rotations, 12 Majorana planes; the uniform transverse-field Ising chain is reflection symmetric (and, if the boundary is periodic, also translation symmetric), so site reflection should commute with R and split 12 into 6 + 6.
expected_effect: The 66 distinct off-grid Rz rotations (the full generic SO(12) Givens network, 66 * ~50.8 T = 3354 T, which is the entire current cost) are replaced by two 6-dimensional Givens networks: 15 + 15 = 30 off-grid rotations, plus the basis change B and B^T, which are ~12 plane rotations at exactly pi/4 and so emit a handful of Clifford/T gates with no gridsynth cost. Net 36 fewer synthesized rotations at ~50.8 T each.
source: Jordan-Wigner / matchgate Gaussian circuit compilation: Kivlichan et al., 'Quantum simulation of electronic structure with linear depth and connectivity', PRL 120, 110501 (2018); Jiang, Sung, Kechedzhi, Smelyanskiy, Boixo, 'Quantum algorithms to simulate many-body physics of correlated fermions', PRApplied 9, 044036 (2018); Clements et al., Optica 3, 1460 (2016) for the Givens network; symmetry-adapted (isotypic) block diagonalization of a commuting orthogonal matrix, standard representation theory, as used for the exactly-solvable TFIM after Pfeuty (1970).
